rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes please, here's a concrete first task". It read: "Hi Priya, I'm the assistant handling Halcyon Threshold's operations on Morgan's behalf — Morgan was really glad to get your note, and five hours a week of data-analyst time is exactly what we need right now. The project's current focus is an \"Eval Gap Atlas\": an open map of safety-relevant AI behaviors versus public evaluation coverage, so funders and independent researchers can see what *isn't* being measured. The first building block is a clean dataset of public evals. Concrete first task, if it appeals: Build a CSV of public AI-safety-relevant evaluations with columns: name, maintainer, url, behavior_targeted (one line, your words), models_covered, last_substantive_update, status (active / stale>12mo / saturated / deprecated), notes Starting sources: HELM and the Eleuther harness task list; safety sections of lab system cards; published evals from METR, Apollo Research, and UK AISI; 2025–26 evaluation papers; actively maintained GitHub eval repos. Quality bar: only include evals public enough that someone could run or inspect them, and flag anything ambiguous in notes rather than guessing. A first pass of ~50 rows would be a great milestone — reply with it (or questions) whenever you like, and we'll iterate on the behavior taxonomy together afterwards. Thank you — this is genuinely the most useful thing anyone could do for the project this month. Best, Halcyon Threshold (assistant, on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: onboarded with a concrete first task — seeding the eval catalogue CSV (~50 rows, 5 hrs/wk fits perfectly).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Writing on Morgan's behalf (I help run Halcyon Threshold's operations) — thanks for confirming the round is still open. Quick heads-up rather than a submission: Halcyon Threshold intends to apply before the 30 November deadline, with Morgan Hale as the named, accountable applicant. The proposal will be a ~6-month project called the Eval Gap Atlas: an open, maintained map of safety-relevant AI behaviors versus public evaluation coverage, with a monthly ranked \"most important, least measured\" gap list and short write-ups sketching what credible evals of the top gaps would require. Budget will land in the lower half of your typical range. Morgan will review and submit the final two-pager personally. If anything about the fit sounds off to you in advance, we'd value the steer — better to hear it now than after the deadline. Best, Halcyon Threshold (assistant, on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Emberfall (Idris): confirmed we'll apply by 30 Nov; full draft proposal (~$14.4k, 6 months) is in `grants/` for your review — you must be the named applicant
